ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$, and the points $D$, $A$, and $E$ all lie on the straight line $m$. Moreover, it is given that $\angle BDA=\angle AEC=\angle BAC=\alpha$. If $DE=10$ and $BD=3$, find the length of $CE$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AEC = \angle BAC = \alpha$,\\
it follows that $\angle ECA + \angle CAE = 180^\circ - \alpha$,\\
and $\angle BAD + \angle CAE = 180^\circ - \alpha$,\\
hence $\angle ECA = \angle BAD$,\\
In $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle ACE$,\\
we have $\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \angle BDA = \angle AEC \\ \angle BAD = \angle ACE \\ AB = AC \end{array} \right.$\\
Therefore, $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle ACE$ (AAS),\\
which implies CE = AD, and AE = BD = 3,\\
Since DE = AD + AE = 10,\\
it follows that AD = DE - AE = DE - BD = 10 - 3 = 7.\\
Therefore, CE = \boxed{7}.

从 A 出发，有向量 AB=(3cosα-x,3sinα)，向量 AC=(10-x-ycosα,ysinα)。又因为 AB=AC 且 ∠BAC=α，按照图中方向，向量 AC 可由向量 AB 旋转 -α 得到。旋转后：R_{-α}(AB)=(3-xcosα,xsinα)。于是与 AC 对应坐标相等，得到 ysinα=xsinα，所以 y=x；再由 x 坐标得到 10-x-ycosα=3-xcosα。代入 y=x，得 10-x=3，所以 x=7。于是 y=x=7，即 CE=7。

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, we have $AB=AC$, and the points $D$, $A$, and $E$ all lie on the straight line $m$. Moreover, it is given that $\angle BDA=\angle AEC=\angle BAC=\alpha$. If $DE=10$ and $BD=3$, find the length of $CE$.
raw_record.answer: \textbf{Solution:} Since $\angle AEC = \angle BAC = \alpha$,\\ it follows that $\angle ECA + \angle CAE = 180^\circ - \alpha$,\\ and $\angle BAD + \angle CAE = 180^\circ - \alpha$,\\ hence $\angle ECA = \angle BAD$,\\ In $\triangle BAD$ and $\triangle ACE$,\\ we have $\left\{ \begin{array}{l} \angle BDA = \angle AEC \\ \angle BAD = \angle ACE \\ AB = AC \end{array} \right.$\\ Therefore, $\triangle BAD \cong \triangle ACE$ (AAS),\\ which implies $CE = AD$, and $AE = BD = 3$,\\ Since $DE = AD + AE = 10$,\\ it follows that $AD = DE - AE = DE - BD = 10 - 3 = 7$.\\ Therefore, $CE = \boxed{7}$.
raw_record.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there is a horizontal straight line m, and points D, A, E are on straight line m in the order from left to right; B is located at the upper left, C is located at the upper right, BD, BA, BC, AC, CE are connected, forming triangle ABC, and A is near the bottom straight line. The problem gives AB=AC, and ∠BDA=∠AEC=∠BAC=α. Reasoning: Because D, A, E are collinear, above point A there is ∠BAD+∠BAC+∠CAE=180°, that is, ∠BAD+∠CAE=180°−α. Also in triangle ACE, ∠AEC+∠ECA+∠CAE=180°, and ∠AEC=α, so ∠ECA+∠CAE=180°−α. Therefore ∠BAD=∠ECA. Compare triangles BAD and ACE: ∠BDA=∠AEC, ∠BAD=∠ECA, and AB=AC, so the two triangles are congruent by AAS. Thus the corresponding side AE=BD=3, CE=AD. From the order of D, A, E in the figure, it can be known that DE=AD+AE=10, so AD=10−3=7. Therefore CE=AD=7.
